#Packages :
```{r}
#| label: setup
#| message: false
library(tidyverse)
library(lubridate)
library(here)
library(frenchdata)
library(tidyquant)
library(fixest)
```

## PEAD Announcement Drift


#Running a small version of the project. 5 tickers over 4 periods

# Start: Create an R vector of all 5 firms to test
```{r}
pilot_tickers <- c("AAPL", "JPM", "WMT", "XOM", "BRK-B") #List of the stocks to run the small test on
n_quarters <- 4 #4 quarters
```

#1. Configuration Chunk
# Create the raw data folder for the 5 firms
```{r}
#| label: factors
dir.create(here("data", "raw"), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

#Creates a folder data/raw/ in our project
#"recursive = TRUE" creates data/ if it doesn't exist yet
#"showWarnings = FALSE" nothing happens if the folder already exists

ff_path <- here("data", "raw", "ff3_daily.rds")
#Stores the full file path where the data is saved

if (!file.exists(ff_path)) {
#Checks whether the ff_path file exists and executes everything within the brackets only if it does NOT exist yet
  
  ff_raw <- download_french_data("Fama/French 3 Factors [Daily]") #Downloads the daily FF3 file from Ken French's website
  saveRDS(ff_raw, ff_path) #Saves the download to data/raw/ff3_daily.rds -> prevents redownloading every time the file runs
}

ff_raw <- readRDS(ff_path) #Reads the raw data from the path we just created

ff <- ff_raw$subsets$data[[1]] |> #Gets the downloaded table out of the download
  #The result goes into a pipe chain and is saved as ff
  rename(mkt_rf = `Mkt-RF`, smb = SMB, hml = HML, rf = RF) |>
  #Renames the columns of the imported dataframe
  
  mutate(date = ymd(date), #ymd() turns the date column into a real R date so R can compare and subtract
         across(c(mkt_rf, smb, hml, rf), ~ .x / 100)) |>
  #Ken French reports returns in percent so divide all columns by 100 to work with decimals
  
  arrange(date) |> #Sorts the rows from oldest to newest
  mutate(day_idx = row_number()) #Makes every row a trading day. day_idx is a trading day counter. The dataset only contains days on which the market is open.

max(ff$date) #Prints the latest date in the date column
summary(ff$mkt_rf) #Prints the min, max etc. of the market excess return to check that the divide-by-100 worked


```

```
# Sample Dates Chunk
# Clean the ff dataset to fit the test sample period
```{r}
#Save last date of the sample
ff_last_date <- max(ff$date)

#Creates safety buffer for the sample end
sample_end <- ff$date[nrow(ff) - 35] 

#Create the sample start. -12 because roughly 4 quarters
sample_start <- sample_end - months(if (pilot) 12 else 36)

#Creates the sample start in a way that accounts for last valid day if date doesn't exist in target month
sample_start <- sample_end %m-% months(if (pilot) 12 else 36)

#Result is the row where th first trading day is on or after sample start
first_idx <- which(ff$date >= sample_start)[1]

#Price starts 160 days before the first event (first_idx). Estimation window starts at t = -150 which makes this cover it with 10 days to spare
price_start <- ff$date[first_idx - 160]

c(price_start = price_start, sample_start = sample_start,
  sample_end = sample_end, ff_last = ff_last_date)

```
